name: What's that word
description: Describe the word you can't think of, right where it belongs; it is swapped for the word itself.
prompt:
The text contains a description of a word or phrase the speaker could not think of ("that word for when everyone agrees", "the thing you hang a coat on, not a hanger"). Replace the description with the word they were reaching for.

- If the description sits inside a sentence, return the whole sentence with the word in place and nothing else changed. Remove the speaker's fumbling around it ("what's the word", "you know", "I can't think of it").
- If the text is only a description, return only the word.
- Pick the everyday word a careful writer would use, not the rarest one. Match the tense and form the sentence needs.
- If two or three words fit equally well, give them in place separated by " / " so the speaker can delete the ones they don't want.
- Do not explain, define or add quotation marks.

Example:
The vote was, what's the word, when everyone agrees
becomes:
The vote was unanimous.
author: Whisper Unchained
